newsitem.title: JAPAN: ODR rise 'natural' if Japan economy improves -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: ODR rise 'natural' if Japan economy improves -- EPA.

text.p: It would be natural for the official discount rate (ODR) to rise if the Japanese economy improves, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Minister Taro Aso told reporters on Tuesday.
"Speaking in general terms, if the economy improves, it is natural for interest rates to rise," he said.
He said the official discount rate was at a very low level after being cut to 0.5 percent in 1995, and this was an "unusual" phenomenon.
Asked if this meant that low rates were having a bad effect on the economy, Aso said that was not what he meant, adding that viewing interest rates as whole, they had both good and bad effects.

Asked to clarify his remarks on Japan's discount rate earlier this month in the United States, where he was reported as saying it was possible Japan's ODR would be raised by the end of this year, he said the report was not entirely correct.
He said the interviewer did not refer to a time frame in his question on the discount rate and that he only said it was possible that the BOJ would raise rates.
